content: We need a retrosynthesis route with 1 reaction that corresponds to a carbonyl-ene reaction (reverse of forward carbonyl-ene). The target molecule: an alkene attached to aromatic ring and a cyclopentanol with CF3 group? Actually structure: CH2= C( aromatic phenyl ) attached to chiral carbon bearing cyclopentanol with CF3. The carbonyl-ene forward would be a ketone reacting with alkene to give product with new C-C bond and OH. So retrosynthesis: break the C-C bond formed in ene, generate a ketone and an alkene (the same molecule maybe intramolecular). So we need a template that does carbonyl-ene reverse: i.e., product (our target) -> precursors: a ketone (maybe a cyclopentanone) and an alkene (the exocyclic double bond). The template likely exists. Search for templates where functional groups broken: aliphatic hydroxyls, five-membered rings; formed: ketones, C-C double bonds. We got empty. Maybe need to search without specifying functional groups formed. Let's search for templates that break aliphatic hydroxyls and five-membered rings.
